EqMatrix¶

This module introduces the EqMatrix class, a class handling all equilibrium matrices and related calculations. It provides methods to calculate the eigensystem and stable solution, as well as a simple checker for detailed balance.

Creating an equilibrium matrix¶

Most of the time, EqMatrix objects will be created through the calc_weq() method. It is possible however to create an EqMatrix as-is.

To create an equilibrium matrix, we declare an EqMartix object. As input one can use either an array like object or an integer. If an integer n is used, EqMatrix will be an empty (n, n) matrix:

>>> from stoch_imp import EqMatrix
>>> print(EqMatrix(3))
⎡0  0  0⎤
⎢       ⎥
⎢0  0  0⎥
⎢       ⎥
⎣0  0  0⎦
>>> print(EqMatrix([[-0.5, 1], [0.5, -1]]))
⎡-0.5  1 ⎤
⎢        ⎥
⎣0.5   -1⎦
>>> print(EqMatrix([[1, 0], [0, 1]]))
ValueError: Column 0 does not sum to 0 (sum = 1.00000000000000)

When creating the equilibrium matrix that is not a valid transfer matrix (non-zero column sums or negative rates) an error will be raised.

Building the system¶

Starting from an empty matrix, interactions can be added by using the add_trans() method. In the code sample we add a transition from site 1 to site 2 with transition rate 2.

>>> from stoch_imp import EqMatrix
>>> weq = EqMatrix(3)
>>> print(weq.add_trans(1, 2, r=2))
⎡-2  1/2   0⎤
⎢           ⎥
⎢2   -1/2  0⎥
⎢           ⎥
⎣0    0    0⎦

Warning

It is generally not advisable to add transitions directly to the matrix using item assignment. Although this can be done, the matrix diagonal needs to be recalculated using calc_diag(). The add_trans() method on the other hand takes care of this for you, along with other quality of life improvements.

Calculating eigensystem¶

After building the system, we can calculate the eigensystem and equilibrium distribution using calc_eig(). These values are then returned and stored as attributes of the object. By default, detailed balance is checked.

Note

The method calc_peq() is basically an alias for calc_eig(). Because the equilibrium distribution is calculated using the eigensystem, the full calculation of the eigensystem is performed to avoid wasting resources.

If the eigensystem is already calculated and a recalculation is needed, you must use the force flag. Otherwise the old values are returned.

Numeric calculations¶

By default, the EqMatrix is treated as a symbolic matrix. If numeric calculations are preferred, use the to_num() to convert the matrix and eigensystem to numeric types. This method does not calculate anything, it merely converts all stored quantities to numeric and changes the type of the matrix. Any future calculations will be done numerically. To convert back to symbolical calculations, use to_sym().

Reference¶

class stoch_imp.EqMatrix.EqMatrix(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Class handling all Equilibrium Transfer Matrices.

This class extends ConstantObject and TrMatrix to provide functionality for equilibrium systems, including eigenvalue/eigenvector computation and equilibrium distribution (peq) calculation.

Variables:

  • mat – Internal sympy.Matrix representation of the transition matrix.

  • dim – Number of rows in the matrix.

  • iter – Iterator over matrix indices.

  • zero_index – Boolean indicating whether 0-based indexing is used.

  • is_symbolic – Boolean indicating whether the matrix is in symbolic form.

  • tol – Numerical tolerance used for validations.

  • nmat – Numeric matrix representation if symbolic flag is False; otherwise None.

  • peq – Equilibrium distribution as a ConstantMatrix, or None if not yet calculated.

  • vals – List of symbolic eigenvalues, or None if not yet calculated.

  • nvals – Numpy array of numeric eigenvalues, or None if not yet calculated.

  • vecs – List of symbolic eigenvectors, or None if not yet calculated.

  • nvecs – Numpy array of numeric eigenvectors, or None if not yet calculated.

add_trans(i, j, r=1.0, ri=None, symm=True, simp=True)¶

Add a transition i –> j with rate r, and optionally symmetric transition j –> i with rate ri.

Parameters:

  • i (int) – Start index

  • j (int) – Target index

  • r (float | Expr) – Transition rate from i to j

  • ri (float | Expr | None) – Optional inverse rate (j to i)

  • symm (bool) – If True, adds j –> i with rate 1/r or ri

  • simp (bool) – If True, simplifies r and ri
